title: Conversation Science Recovery — Wave 005: Hidden Models Beyond Named Theories
mission: Search old conversation/library material not only for named theories but for unnamed mathematical scaffolds, repeated relation grammars, numerical fragments and equations hidden inside symbolic, theological, body, astronomy and cultural discussions.
search_methods_used: Named-theory search: 11D Axis, M-theory, field, unified, supersymmetry, quarks, torus, precession.
Operator search: Door, projection, ladder, threshold, handshake, mirror, frame crossing, funnel, drain, attractor, spiral, return, collapse.
Directional-polarity search: up/down, advanced/retarded, past/future, alpha/omega, vertical/horizontal, inner/outer, macro/micro.
Equation-signature search: pi_d, R_d, F_d, D_eff, Box^alpha, quark fractions, qutrit/qubit, torus circumference, phase shift, angle, 90 degree.
Number archaeology: 33, 26,000, 115,000, 100,000, 1.3, 5D, 11D; then separate quantities with different units.
Date-window archaeology: inspect periods where public/project vocabulary changed before technical language appeared.
Repository-gap inversion: search the Library for items that existing GitHub documents list only as unresolved recovery targets.
Alias search: search conceptual neighbors when exact names may not have existed yet (e.g. future/past instead of advanced/retarded; frame/wedge/needle instead of Door).
Prose-to-model extraction: identify repeated relation patterns in long symbolic prose, then formalize only after preserving provenance.

next_skim_strategy: Search typo variants and raw-number fragments, not only normalized vocabulary.
Search old chats around one or two days before/after every first attestation date, because equations are often introduced before names stabilize.
Search image/diagram references and ASCII tables; models may survive as diagrams without equations.
Search for equations by operators/symbols rather than theory names: psi, ket, bra, sigma, theta, phi, pi, tensor, cross product, determinant, Hamiltonian, Lagrangian, metric.
Search creative and theology threads for embedded mathematics because Great Book/Axis equations repeatedly appeared outside science-specific conversations.
Compare assistant-generated summaries with raw user lines to recover the initiating user intuition and avoid backdating assistant notation.
Maintain a negative-evidence ledger so unresolved remembered calculations remain visible without being reconstructed from guesswork.
